# Serving-side authentication and authorization

Read when the service establishes caller identity or access. The server is the boundary; client-side
guards are only UX.

- Match the organization's identity/session protocol. Validate credentials on every protected route,
  including issuer/audience/expiry and replay properties required by that protocol.
- Authorize the action on the specific resource. Authentication alone is not object-level or
  tenant-level authorization. Deny by default and keep scopes/roles least privilege.
- Choose browser sessions, bearer tokens, refresh, logout, and revocation as one threat-modeled
  contract; do not prescribe a refresh cookie or JWT when the loaded platform uses another design.
- Machine callers use scoped, attributable, rotatable identities—not a shared administrator token.
- Use the repository's maintained password library and its current Argon2id-recommended configuration
  for new hashes. Verify supported legacy hashes, rehash after successful authentication when
  obsolete, and migrate bcrypt deliberately. Perform a dummy verification for unknown users to reduce
  username-timing differences.
- Rate-limit credential and recovery endpoints, prevent account enumeration, and keep credentials,
  tokens, session IDs, reset links, and auth payloads out of logs.
- Auth, token, crypto, cookie, and untrusted-input boundary changes require an independent security
  review with failure-path tests.
